equity_bridge.item: H1 FY2026 cash generation already reflected in 30-Jun-2026 net debt (Y1 flows cover the full FY2026)
equity_bridge.note: H1 FY2026 interim report, summary cash flow: net debt fell from $2,074.8M (31 Dec 2025) to $1,720.0M (30 Jun 2026). Deducted so the windfall half-year is counted once.

historical_growth.growth_rate_source: revenue_3yr_cagr (FY2022-FY2025), rounded; equity CAGR rejected as a growth basis
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity CAGR (-15.4% 3yr, -7.1% 5yr) diverges from revenue (+2.6% 3yr) by far more than 30pp. Book value shrank because of inventory-revaluation statutory losses (FY2024 -$76M, FY2025 -$421M), dividends and buybacks, not because the operating business shrank; it is not a growth signal. EPS CAGRs are undefined (negative statutory EPS at both FY2024 and FY2025 endpoints). Owner-FCF CAGRs are undefined: owner FCF after lease principal was -88 (FY2020), +198 (FY2021), +631 (FY2022), -27 (FY2023), -262 (FY2024), -155 (FY2025), negative at both endpoints because FY2023-25 was the acquisition-and-capex phase (Coles Express, OTR, Liberty, ULSG plant). The 5yr revenue CAGR of 18.1% is off the COVID-depressed FY2020 base and is not forward-relevant.
historical_growth.notes: Owner-FCF series = reported FCF - SBC - lease principal (treatment B; interest income not stripped, net borrower). Reported FCF (OCF - capex) looked positive in every year because IFRS 16 moved $125-299M/yr of lease principal below the FCF line; the owner-FCF series removes that flattering. Underlying EBITDA (RC), the series the forward margins are anchored to: FY2020 245, FY2021 484, FY2022 1,076, FY2023 713, FY2024 749, FY2025 701, H1 FY2026 774 (FY2026E ~1,150).

scenario_narratives.base: The FY2026 windfall is real cash (H1 FY2026 EBITDA (RC) $774M, net debt down $355M to $1.72bn) but not a run-rate: the Geelong Refining Margin of US$21.1/bbl was driven by Middle East supply disruption and management expects it to moderate in 2H26. Base assumes FY2026 EBITDA (RC) ~A$1,150M, FY2027 ~900M, then a mid-cycle ~840M (2.7% of revenue, below the FY2021-25 average of 3.0%) growing ~2.5%/yr nominal. C&M grows modestly off its FY2025 trough ($197M to ~$270M) as the OTR/Reddy Express/Liberty integration cost duplication rolls off; C&I holds ~$490M on its multi-decade contract base; E&I earns ~$130M at a US$9-10/bbl GRM with the ULSG premium and the FSSP floor. Capex settles at ~A$370-440M after the ULSG/ERP/Liberty programme, cash tax ramps from 10% to 30% as the $519M net DTA is consumed, lease costs stay inside EBITDA (RC). Horizon 10 years, terminal cap 13x owner FCF.
scenario_narratives.bull: Regional refining margins stay structurally tighter after the 2026 disruption (closures elsewhere, ULSG specification premium), the FSSP is renegotiated favourably, Geelong availability recovers to >90%, and the C&M strategy finally delivers (~$330M EBITDA (RC)) through OTR conversions, Flybuys/digital loyalty and an owned convenience supply chain; C&I adds renewable diesel/SAF and specialty volumes. Mid-cycle EBITDA (RC) ~A$980M, margin drifting to 3.2% as the convenience mix rises. Deleveraging to <1.5x funds a step-up in fully franked dividends. Terminal growth 2.5%, cap 14x.
scenario_narratives.bear: The refining windfall unwinds within 18 months, and the Alkylation fire proved how quickly a single-site refinery can lose output. C&M never reaches target (tobacco -17%, illicit trade, retail crime, leadership churn after the C&M CEO exit), C&I loses its disruption-era hedging gains, and Geelong runs at a GRM of ~US$7/bbl where the FSSP prevents a loss but little more. EV uptake and NVES erode petrol volumes from the late 2020s, and the Vitol exclusive supply renewal in 2028 becomes a governance fight. Mid-cycle EBITDA (RC) ~A$640M, margin eroding to 2.1%, terminal growth 0.5%, cap 11x: a business in slow run-off still carrying $1.7bn of net debt and $3.6bn of leases.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Value Viva as a mid-cycle integrated fuel supplier, not on FY2026 earnings. The refining windfall is banked in net debt where it belongs (the 30 June 2026 balance sheet, with the H1 double count removed via the bridge), and the forward margin path fades the windfall out over two years before capitalising a mid-cycle EBITDA (RC) that sits below the five-year average margin. Leases are treated once, as an operating cost inside EBITDA (RC), so the $3.6bn lease liability is not also deducted as debt. SBC is immaterial (~0.03% of revenue) so house and street values nearly coincide. Risk is charged once, in the scenario flows and the 30/50/20 weights, not in a scenario-specific WACC. The terminal cap (11-14x owner FCF) keeps the Gordon value from assuming a multiple no buyer pays for a refiner.
key_risks_to_valuation: Mid-cycle refining margin: every US$1/bbl on ~38 MMbbl of intake is roughly A$55-60M of EBITDA; the base assumes US$9-10/bbl against US$21 in H1 FY2026 and US$7-8 in weak years.
C&M delivery: the base assumes only a partial recovery to ~A$270M; the gap to management's original ambition is the main bull-case lever and the main source of past disappointment.
Single-refinery outages (April 2026 Alkylation fire, January 2025 lightning shutdown) and FSSP renegotiation outcome.
Capex run-rate: base assumes ~A$370-440M; a return to the FY2023-25 integration-phase average of ~A$550M would remove most of the owner FCF.
Structural fuel demand decline from EV adoption and NVES, and the 2028 Vitol exclusive supply renewal.
Leverage: net debt A$1.72bn plus A$3.6bn of lease liabilities; the valuation treats leases as operating cost but the fixed-charge burden is real in a downturn.

data_sources.price: Yahoo Finance chart API regular close at inputs.price_as_of; 52-week range 1.695-3.28.
data_sources.financials: VEA.AX_Metrics.csv (core_metrics, FY2018-FY2025 annual and H1 FY2018-H1 FY2026 interim, AUD millions); FY2025 annual report (five-year summary, segment EBITDA (RC) reconciliation, net debt note, lease note, EPS note, shareholder information); H1 FY2026 interim report (net debt note 13, equity note 14, summary cash flow, segment EBITDA (RC) reconciliation, capex by segment).
data_sources.qualitative: VEA.AX_Analysis.json (2026-11-08): segment commentary, 1H2026 results and July 2026 trading update, FY2026 capex and store-rollout guidance, risks (refining cyclicality, C&M execution, single-refinery concentration, Vitol renewal, EV/NVES).

inputs.share_count_basis: 1,642,520,936 ordinary shares at 30 June 2026 (H1 FY2026 interim report, note 14) plus 6,571,235 unquoted LTI performance rights (FY2025 annual report shareholder information, 28 Jan 2026) = 1,649.1M fully diluted. Held FLAT: SBC is expensed in the flows. The DRP issued ~15-17M shares/yr in FY2025-26 (~1%/yr); that is optional dividend reinvestment, not compensation, and the retained cash lands in net debt, so it is treated as value-neutral rather than compounded into the count.
inputs.sbc_source: FY2025 annual report, statement of changes in equity / cash-flow non-cash items: share-based payment expense $7.8M (FY2024 $14.7M). Equity-award taxes nil (Australian net-settlement withholding not disclosed as a separate financing line). Interest income ($10.2M) NOT deducted: the company is a net borrower, no cash pile is added to EV.
inputs.wacc_rationale: AUD flows discounted at an AUD-built WACC. Risk-free: 10-year ACGB ~4.4%; ERP 5.5%; equity beta ~1.05 (integrated fuel refiner/retailer, ASX peer Ampol) gives cost of equity ~10.2%. Pre-tax cost of debt ~6.3% (RCF + term loan margins over BBSW), 30% tax gives ~4.4% after tax. Market weights: equity A$4.4bn, net debt ex-leases A$1.7bn -> D/(D+E) ~28%. WACC = 0.72 x 10.2% + 0.28 x 4.4% = 8.6%, rounded to 8.5%. The SAME WACC is used in all three scenarios: refining-margin cyclicality, C&M execution risk and single-refinery concentration are charged in the scenario flows and the probability weights, not stacked into the discount rate.
inputs.lease_treatment: Treatment (B), leases as operating cost. Viva's underlying EBITDA (RC) is defined on the superseded AASB 117 basis, i.e. lease expense is already deducted inside it (FY2025 lease expense $495.3M vs cash lease payments of $522.9M = principal $299.3M + interest $223.6M; H1 FY2026 $256.2M vs $247.9M cash). The EBITDA margin path is therefore the EBITDA (RC) margin, lease_cost_pct_path is held at 0 so the lease is not charged twice, lease liabilities ($3,608.8M at 30 June 2026) are EXCLUDED from net debt, and D&A for the tax line is ex right-of-use depreciation (FY2025: $604.7M total less $347.9M ROU = $256.8M, 0.90% of revenue). last_fcf is the FY2025 owner FCF on the same basis: reported FCF 151.7 - SBC 7.8 - lease principal 299.3 = -155.4 (FY2025 was a peak-capex year: $557.5M gross capex on ULSG, ERP and Liberty integration).
inputs.nci_treatment: No material non-controlling interest (FY2025 annual report: associates only). Flows are 100% attributable; no NCI deduction in the bridge.
inputs.notes: Model: owner-FCF DCF, component build, via the Drivers route (SKILL.md routing row: operating company, non-US and cyclical, with the adaptations for AUD WACC, IFRS 16 leases and charging risk once). Chosen because Viva is an operating business (refining + convenience retail + commercial fuels) whose value is a stream of free cash flow; it is not a bank, REIT or holdco. First valuation of this ticker (no memory entry). PEAK-EARNINGS GUARD: FY2026 earnings carry a refining-margin windfall (GRM US$21.1/bbl in H1 FY2026 vs US$8.2/bbl pcp, Middle East supply disruption) that management says will moderate in 2H26. Year 1 (FY2026) uses the elevated margin, year 2 fades it, and year 3 onward sits on a mid-cycle EBITDA (RC) of ~A$840M (2.7% of revenue), BELOW the FY2021-25 average margin of 3.0% and against FY2023-25 actuals of 713/749/701. Terminal value capitalises the mid-cycle margin, never the windfall. TIMING: Y1 flows span the whole of FY2026 while net debt is the 30 June 2026 figure, which already contains H1's cash generation; the -354.8 equity_bridge item (H1 FY2026 net-debt reduction) removes that double count. Sanity multiples must be lease-consistent: ex-lease EV (~A$6.1bn at the current price) against EBITDA (RC) which is post-lease (~7.3x mid-cycle), or lease-inclusive EV against post-IFRS-16 EBITDA; never ex-lease EV over IFRS-16 EBITDA. Revenue is price-driven (fuel is a pass-through commodity), so revenue growth here means product-price plus volume drift and the EBITDA margin paths are calibrated to absolute EBITDA (RC) targets per segment, stated in the scenario narratives. Statutory (historical-cost) EBITDA, net income and EPS are dominated by inventory revaluation (FY2025 statutory loss -$421M vs NPAT (RC) +$184M) and are not used.

bear.ebitda_margin_note: FY2026E ~A$1,035M (weaker H2: margins fade faster, residual Alkylation-fire impact). FY2027 ~655 as product prices and margins collapse back. Mid-cycle ~640 from FY2028: C&M stuck ~220 (integration never reaches target, tobacco/illicit trade and crime drag), C&I ~450 (hedging gains gone, mining/aviation softness), E&I ~25 (GRM ~US$7/bbl, outages, Safeguard costs; FSSP prevents a loss but the refinery is marginal), corporate -55. Margin erodes to 2.1% as EV/NVES fuel demand decline bites.
bear.capex_note: Slightly higher sustaining capex: refinery integrity spend after the 2026 fire and Safeguard Mechanism compliance.
bear.narrative: Refining margin tailwind reverses hard, C&M execution keeps missing, Geelong becomes marginal (FSSP floor only), structural fuel-demand decline sets in and the Vitol supply renewal (2028) is contested. Terminal growth 0.5% and an 11x cap reflect a business in slow run-off. Same WACC as base.

base.growth_note: FY2026 +12% is H1 actual (+10.2% YoY on higher product prices, 16,487.5) plus a moderating H2; FY2027 -4% as product prices and regional margins normalise; then ~2-2.5% nominal (volumes flat to slightly down on EV/NVES erosion, convenience and C&I specialty growth, modest inflation).
base.ebitda_margin_note: EBITDA (RC), post-lease. FY2026E ~A$1,150M = H1 actual 774.4 + H2 ~375 (management: refining drivers moderate in 2H26; hedging gains not recurring). FY2027 ~900 as GRM fades toward mid-cycle. FY2028+ mid-cycle ~840: C&M ~270 (H1 FY2026 annualised, modest growth), C&I ~490 (FY2025 460.5 plus Karratha/specialty growth, ex-disruption hedging gains), E&I ~130 at GRM ~US$9-10/bbl with ULSG premium and FSSP floor, corporate -52. Compare FY2023-25 actuals 713/749/701 and the FY2021-25 average margin of 3.0%.
base.lease_cost_note: Zero by construction: lease expense is already inside EBITDA (RC) (AASB 117 basis). See inputs.lease_treatment.
base.da_note: D&A ex right-of-use depreciation: FY2025 $256.8M = 0.90% of revenue; 0.85% on the higher FY2026 revenue base.
base.capex_note: FY2026 guidance A$350-400M (reaffirmed at 1H2026; H1 actual $127.2M) = 1.17% of FY2026E revenue. Thereafter ~1.2% (~A$370-440M) covering refinery turnarounds and base retail network capex plus 20-25 OTR openings/yr; well above D&A ex-ROU, below the FY2023-25 integration-phase average of $546M.
base.cash_tax_note: Australian statutory 30%. Net deferred tax assets of $518.8M at 31 Dec 2025 (tax losses from FY2024-25 statutory losses, ULSG and acquisition deductions) and only $25.1M cash tax paid in H1 FY2026 justify a ramp: 10% FY2026, 18% FY2027, 25% FY2028, 30% thereafter.
base.wc_note: Fuel distributor: hydrocarbon payables broadly fund inventory and receivables; working-capital swings are price-timing noise (H1 FY2026 -$278M, FY2025 +$145M). No structural capture assumed in either direction.
base.narrative: Mid-cycle integrated fuel supplier: refining windfall fades over FY2026-27, C&M delivers modest growth off the FY2025 trough, C&I compounds slowly, Geelong runs at mid-cycle margins with FSSP support. Terminal cap 13x owner FCF (cyclical, within the house 12-15x range).

bull.ebitda_margin_note: FY2026E ~A$1,210M (H2 refining stays strong; GRM July US$20.7/bbl). Regional margins remain structurally elevated into FY2027 (~1,000). Mid-cycle ~980 by FY2028-29: C&M reaches ~330 as the OTR conversion/loyalty/own-supply-chain strategy finally delivers, C&I ~520 with renewable diesel/SAF and specialty growth, E&I ~180 with ULSG premium, a renegotiated FSSP and higher availability, corporate -50. Margin drifts to 3.2% as the convenience mix rises.
bull.narrative: C&M strategy delivers, regional refining margins stay structurally tighter post-2026 disruption, FSSP renegotiated favourably, deleveraging funds higher dividends. Same WACC as base: the upside is in the flows.

required_return_table.note: Each row rebuilds the terminal value at that row's rate (max(0, min(Gordon@r, 13x FCF_N))); the WACC row is valuation.base.intrinsic_value and the hurdle row is entry_price.base.entry_price.

sensitivity.note: Rows are WACC, columns terminal growth; each cell rebuilds its own terminal value.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Moved from the house default 15/50/35 to 30/50/20. Bear weight up because the earnings base is cyclical and currently inflated by a geopolitical windfall, C&M has missed management's own targets for several years (nil LTI vesting, forfeited STIs, C&M CEO exit), the Group depends on a single 120-year-old refinery that caught fire in April 2026, net debt is still ~2.4x mid-cycle EBITDA (RC) with $3.6bn of leases on top, and the Vitol supply agreement renewal in 2028 is a live governance overhang. Bull weight down because the bull case needs several independent things to go right at once (structurally higher refining margins, a favourable FSSP outcome, and a C&M turnaround that has not yet shown up in the numbers).

sanity_check.basis: SBC-adjusted on both sides (EPS less SBC/share; EBITDA less SBC), so these deliberately do not match GAAP screener multiples.
